relevance_note: The paper describes four individual HA20 patients in two Japanese families with TNFAIP3 variants: "Four HA20 patients in the two families presented with childhood-onset recurrent oral and genital ulcers".
method_note: Built with a short Python script in my scratch directory; every value was chosen by reading the paper, and a script check confirmed every span verbatim (spaces normalised to the paper's own thin/no-break spaces). Table 1 has patients as columns; the column header row is '| Patient | Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Patient 3 | Patient 4 |', so spans quote each row from its label through the patient's cell. Table 1 '+' cells were read as present; Table 1 '–' cells are not defined as absent in the legend, so they were recorded as not reported (no rows), and only explicit text absences were used. Scope: Patients 1–4 (variant carriers) plus relatives described as affected (III-1, II-5 and II-2 of family 1) or tested (the parent of Patient 3 who underwent WES; result not stated; the paper never states this parent's sex). The pedigree labels III-1 and II-2 occur in both families (Patient 3 is III-1 and Patient 4 is II-2 in Fig. 1b), so the family 1 relatives are labelled 'III-1 (Family 1)' and 'II-2 (Family 1)'. Left out as neither tested nor affected: the proband's mother in family 1 (II-6, 'no BD-like symptoms', died of colon cancer) and the other maternal relatives in family 2 (I-1, I-2, II-3, II-4, 'no BD-like symptoms'). Table 2, Table S1 and Table S2 give group-level data on 54 (or 26 Japanese) HA20 patients from refs 5–15 plus these four; no individual-level data on previously reported patients, so no rows; the 520 BD cohort patients are out of scope. No stacked ' / ' cells with per-patient values (the ' / ' in Table S1/S2 headers are not patient values). Zygosity 'heterozygous' for the c.1434C>A variant comes from the Introduction sentence 'We here report a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant', which refers to the paper's only single-nucleotide variant; the deletion's zygosity is not stated in text, so it is not reported. Inheritance for Patient 3 is 'inherited maternal' because quantitative PCR confirmed the deletion in her mother (Patient 4). No inheritance for Patients 1/2: the affected father (II-5) was not reported as tested. Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' for the deletion comes from 'Two novel TNFAIP3 pathogenic changes were found in two families', a statement naming both families' variants. Contradiction-like issue: Table 1 gives Fever '–' for Patient 4, while the text says she 'presented fever with tonsillitis and lymphadenitis several times a year since her childhood'; the abstract counts recurrent fever in three of four patients. Because '–' is undefined, I recorded fever as observed from the text and set checklist 'recurrent fever' observed; a reviewer may disagree. Normal investigations ('colonoscopy did not identify any abnormality' for Patient 3 at about 5 years; 'Colonoscopy at 18 years of age did not show any abnormality' for Patient 4) are written as 'colonoscopy abnormality' excluded and exclude nothing more specific; Patient 3's later endoscopy found multiple intestinal ulcers. Patient 2 onset for oral and genital ulcers comes from one sentence ('at 12 and 15 years of age, respectively'), so onset_original_text repeats that phrase and onset_iso8601 differs (P12Y, P15Y). II-5's amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is recorded as a feature, but the checklist item 'central nervous system involvement' is left not reported for him. Broad absences 'did not show any ophthalmological or neurological symptoms' were used to exclude uveitis and CNS involvement (Patients 1 and 4) and 'musculoskeletal symptoms' to exclude arthritis or arthralgia (Patient 4). Table 1 'Age' was taken as age at last evaluation (consistent with the text, e.g. 'a 35-year-old male'). Study inclusion criteria (all patients met the 1987 Japanese BD criteria) were not used as evidence.
